## visual dubbing for real production footage


traditional dubbing replaces the audio while the original mouth shapes remain on screen. sync. regenerates visible speech against new dialogue at the shot level.


### preserve shot continuity


sync-3 uses scene-level context from the selected take to preserve facial performance, timing, lighting, framing, and continuity as the dialogue changes.


### handle edge-case footage


sync-3 is built for production footage with profiles, occlusions, low light, fast motion, close detail, and other conditions that can break simpler lip-sync models.


### fit the finishing pipeline


zero-shot generation removes character-specific training, so sync-3 can move from replacement dialogue to shot-level review without adding a model-training step.


## match each dialogue change to the right model


### rewrite an existing line


use sync-3 to replace spoken dialogue while keeping the performance, lighting, framing, and surrounding scene context intact.


### keep close-up detail natural


for tighter framing, lipsync-2-pro adds a higher-detail pass designed to keep facial definition and polish unchanged around the new dialogue.


### reshape the delivery


react-1 can extend the edit into facial expression and head movement when the performance needs to change along with the words.


## keep more creative options open after capture


visual dubbing gives teams more freedom to revise dialogue, language, and delivery after production while preserving footage already captured.


-


**revise the script** — change a spoken line after the scene has already been filmed.


-


**create new versions** — adapt the same footage for alternate lines or languages.


-


**protect strong takes** — keep a performance that works even when the dialogue changes.


## sync. visual dubbing


existing footage and new dialogue move through model generation, creative review, and delivery inside the post-production workflow.


### where we integrate


-


**pre-color, post-VFX** — receive selected footage and replacement dialogue


-


**post-DI, pre-release** — work from the updated picture for review and delivery


### QC rounds


1.


**visual dubbing pass** — review how the new dialogue reads across selected shots


2.


**near-final frame** — tighten flagged shots against consolidated creative notes


3.


**final delivery** — apply approved revisions and prepare the final outputs


## production formats stay production-ready


sync. models support the formats, color pipelines, and delivery controls professional teams need from source through final output.


-


**ProRes codec support** — work with 4444 XQ through 422 Proxy in post pipelines


-


**OpenEXR image sequences** — support image-sequence workflows alongside video delivery


-


**UHD and 4K DCI output** — keep resolution aligned with professional finishing needs


-


**lossless preservation** — retain bitrate, metadata, and resolution across deliverables


-


**HDR10 and ACES color** — support HDR10, ACES, and Rec.709 color workflows


-


**flexible storage delivery** — use client-side storage or managed private S3 infrastructure


-


**pipeline integrations** — work through Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or API


## choose how you create


six ways to create, localize, and edit video based on the control your project needs.


-


**lipsync video** — match any voice or take to existing footage with natural lip sync across every frame


-


**translate & dub** — turn finished video into new language versions with translated audio and visual sync


-


**edit appearance** — change facial appearance and on-screen looks while preserving the original shot


-


**image to video** — turn a still image into a speaking video by pairing the photo with new dialogue or audio


-


**edit dialogue** — replace any spoken line in existing footage while keeping the original take in the scene


-


**timeline editor** — control dialogue, timing, speakers, and edits on a frame-level timeline for complex work


## visual dubbing in production


For the Malayalam release of *Don’t Trouble the Trouble* , the production team supplied the dubbed audio. sync. labs adapted the visible speech across roughly 800 shots during a 10-day production sprint.


[see the Malayalam performance in the published case study](https://sync.so/blog/dont-trouble-the-trouble-malayalam-visual-dubbing)
